newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Would-be Kohl challenger casts doubt on timely EMU.
newsitem.headline: Would-be Kohl challenger casts doubt on timely EMU.

text.p: Gerhard Schroeder, a leading member of Germany's Social Democrat (SPD) opposition party and widely tipped as a rival for Chancellor Helmut Kohl, has thrown fresh doubt on the feasability of a 1999 Euro launch.

In a guest commentary in the "Europa Journal" magazine, Schroeder warned against any attempts to soften the rules governing the Euro launch and said Germans remained unconvinced that the new currency could be as stable as the deutschmark.
"The success of the Euro is more important than the timetable," Schroeder told the bi-weekly magazine, in a column released ahead of scheduled publication on Tuesday.
"What would be so terrible if the Euro were to arrive three or five years later, but into (what would then be) a politically prepared environment?," he wrote.

Schroeder, the SPD premier of the state of Lower Saxony, has repeatedly questioned the current race toward Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) -- an attitude which has in the past prompted German Finance Minister Theo Waigel to dismiss him as a "baseless oppportunist."

His latest comments come as Kohl fends off public outrage over last week's release of Germany's worst-ever jobless data since the 1930s depression -- which showed that 4.66 million, or 12.2 percent of the workforce, now unemployed.

The report has sparked the first serious doubts that Germany will be in a position to fulfil the budgetary criteria required to take part in the first stage of the Euro launch, planned for January 1999.
However German leaders have downplayed such worries, saying forthcoming tax, pension and labour reforms should ease unemployment problems.
Kohl himself has said he is sticking to Germany's goal of halving joblessness by the year 2000 and Waigel said on Saturday that Germany still had every chance of making the EMU budgetary grade.
Meanwhile, Schroeder denied charges from rivals that he is fundamentally opposed to closer European integration.
"I wonder why anyone who makes critical observations on the Euro is immediately declared an opponent of Europe?," he wrote.
"I also ask why many Euro supporters are in such a hurry to introduce the new currency."
